What are the appropriate ways to schmooze at a company event (as in, to try and get a better job) without pissing off the people you currently work for, but also the people you are asking?

This assumes you're just trying to be generally better about schmoozing, and you're not targeting someone (e.g.: your boss or something):

My old go-to when i comes to conversation is to "yes and..." them, similar to what improve comedians do (but not exactly). Get them to say something - anything really - and then ask them for more information about that topic/event/etc. Example: They mention something about a sports team. You follow up with something along the lines of "I haven't been following them very closely this year - how's the team doing? Do they have what it takes?". Regardless of what they say, ask why. That kind of thing.

It's easier, of course, if the topic is something you have some level of existing knowledge in, but with a little practice, you can use this method to develop almost any conversational thread. Ultimately, the goal is not to become sports-buddies with this person or whatever the thread was, but engage them in something deeper than "how are you" or "how about that weather". Practice genuinely focusing/listening to them - don't just be waiting for your next chance to talk. Be personable, someone they can talk to/talk with.
